extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners (attorneys/agents), Office of Enrollment and Discipline (OED) staff, and others subject to USPTO disciplinary rules
extracted.subtask_description: Standards, procedural rules, and sanctions governing practice before the United States Patent and Trademark Office, including prohibitions on unauthorized practice while excluded, misconduct rules (e.g., false statements), reinstatement requirements, publication of orders, and use of disciplinary records in future proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdiction for USPTO disciplinary proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The Acting USPTO Director has jurisdiction over this matter pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32 and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.19 and 11.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disciplinary authority derives from specific statutes and implementing regulations; proceedings are brought under 35 U.S.C. § 32 and the cited regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility and Disciplinary Rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is subject to the USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility and Disciplinary Rules set forth at 37 C.F.R. § 10.20 et seq.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registered practitioners before the Office are bound by Part 10 ethics/disciplines; citations to these rules form basis for allegations and disciplinary action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on unauthorized practice while excluded
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner who is excluded from practice before the Office shall not engage in the unauthorized practice of patent, trademark, and other non-patent law before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules in effect at the time of exclusion proscribe any practice before the Office by an excluded practitioner; alleged breaches can lead to disciplinary complaints and sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to seek reinstatement under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner previously excluded must seek reinstatement to practice before the Office under applicable statute or rules; Respondent had not sought reinstatement under any section of the patent statute or rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any application for reinstatement must comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.60; the Final Order specifies eligibility timing (e.g., earliest date to apply) and requires full compliance with § 11.60 upon any request for reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on conduct prejudicial to the administration of justice (37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(5) proscribes engaging in conduct prejudicial to the administration of justice; OED considered Respondent's statement to be a false or misleading statement in violation of this rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: False or misleading statements during an OED investigation (for example, misrepresenting compliance with a prior Final Order) may constitute conduct prejudicial to the administration of justice and form the basis for discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other alleged disciplinary rule violations (37 C.F.R. §§ 10.23(a), 10.23(b)(4), 10.23(b)(6), 10.89(c)(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: OED filed a disciplinary complaint alleging violations of 37 C.F.R. §§ 10.23(a); 10.23(b)(4); 10.23(b)(5); 10.23(b)(6); and 10.89(c)(6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the Final Order discusses only § 10.23(b)(5) in detail, a range of Part 10 rules (including those cited) may be charged in disciplinary actions; each cited provision provides independent grounds for complaint and sanction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions: suspension and computation of reinstatement eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall be suspended from practice before the Office in patent, trademark, and other non-patent matters for one year in addition to the previous five-year exclusion, such that Respondent shall be eligible to apply for reinstatement under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 no earlier than six years from November 3, 2007.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discipline can extend existing exclusions; the Final Order demonstrates how multiple exclusionary periods combine to set the earliest date for reinstatement eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligations under 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 and OED obligations under § 11.59
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58; the OED Director shall comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.59.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order expressly imposes compliance obligations on both the disciplined practitioner and the OED consistent with the cited regulations (the Order does not restate the text of those sections but mandates adherence).

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic publication of Final Order in OED FOIA Reading Room
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall electronically publish this Final Order at the OED's electronic FOIA Reading Room, publicly accessible through the Office's website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disciplinary orders are to be posted publicly in the OED reading room; publication increases transparency and public record of disciplinary actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official Gazette notice content and publication
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish a notice in the Official Gazette describing the suspension, identifying the practitioner, stating the basis (violation of 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(5)), and indicating where disciplinary decisions are posted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Official Gazette notice must include identity, registration number, suspension details, basis for discipline, and reference to the OED FOIA Reading Room; the Order provides an explicit example of required notice language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of disciplinary record in future Office proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the Agreement or Final Order prevents the Office from considering the record of this disciplinary proceeding when addressing further complaints or evidence of the same or similar misconduct; in future disciplinary proceedings as an aggravating factor and/or to rebut statements; and when considering any request for reconsideration under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Past disciplinary records may be used by the Office to inform sanctions, rebut representations, and decide reinstatement or reconsideration requests; the Order enumerates specific ways the record may be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural requirement to move to dismiss pending proceedings after settlement
rubrics_metrics.description: Within thirty-five (35) days of the date of this Final Order, the parties shall submit a joint motion to dismiss the USPTO disciplinary proceeding pending against Respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Settlement agreements often require procedural follow-through (e.g., filing a joint motion to dismiss) within a specified timeframe.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of costs in settlement
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director and Respondent shall each bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of this Agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Settlement terms may specify that each side bears its own costs rather than ordering payment of costs or fines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlement approval and binding Final Order
rubrics_metrics.description: The Proposed Settlement Agreement, which resolves all disciplinary action by the USPTO arising from the stipulated facts, is approved and set forth in this Final Order; Respondent acknowledges facts and the legal conclusion supporting the violation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A settlement agreement that is approved by the Acting USPTO Director becomes a Final Order setting forth stipulated facts, legal conclusions, and sanctions; practitioners may consent to facts and sanction terms as part of settlement.

rubrics_metrics.name: OED investigatory process leading to discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: An OED Staff Attorney may mail a 'REQUEST FOR STATEMENT OF RESPONDENT'S POSITION' during an investigation; responses construed as false or misleading can trigger a disciplinary complaint under 35 U.S.C. § 32.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners should take investigatory requests seriously and avoid making false or misleading statements in responses, as such statements may form the basis for disciplinary complaints and proceedings.
